# Rationale of the module today


```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-agent_basic
%%| fig-cap: Simplified classification

flowchart TD
    A[Define the research or analysis goal] --> B[Describe the task to the AI assistant]

    B --> C[AI proposes an approach]
    C --> D[AI generates or modifies R code]
    D --> E[Run the code in RStudio]

    E --> F{Does the code run?}

    F -- No --> G[Give the error and relevant context to the AI]
    G --> C

    F -- Yes --> H{Is the method scientifically valid?}

    H -- No --> I[Review assumptions, data and analytical method]
    I --> B

    H -- Yes --> J[Inspect plots, tables and model diagnostics]

    J --> K{Does the output answer the research question?}

    K -- No --> L[Refine the prompt or analytical approach]
    L --> B

    K -- Yes --> M[Refactor and simplify the code]
    M --> N[Add tests, comments and documentation]
    N --> O[Save code, outputs and session information]
    O --> P[Produce reproducible research output]

    classDef human fill:#d9eaf7,stroke:#2f5597,color:#000;
    classDef ai fill:#fce4d6,stroke:#c65911,color:#000;
    classDef decision fill:#fff2cc,stroke:#bf9000,color:#000;
    classDef output fill:#e2f0d9,stroke:#548235,color:#000;

    class A,B,E,G,I,J,L human;
    class C,D,M,N ai;
    class F,H,K decision;
    class O,P output;

```


-------

# QGIS is great...why use R then?

| Reason | Why it matters |
|:--|:--|
| Reproducibility | R code records each transformation, parameter and analytical decision, making the spatial workflow easier to reproduce and audit. |
| Automation | A scripted workflow can be rerun when input data change, without manually repeating each GIS operation. |
| Scalability | The same analysis can be applied consistently across many species, sites, catchments or input files. |
| Statistical integration | Spatial processing can flow directly into modelling, prediction, diagnostics and uncertainty analysis within the same environment. |
| Reporting integration | Maps, figures, tables and results can be generated directly in a Quarto report. |
| Reuse | Repeated spatial operations can be converted into functions or incorporated into an R package. |
| AI-assisted accessibility | Vibe-coding reduces the syntax barrier by translating a description of the spatial task into candidate R code. |
| Extensibility | Once the initial workflow works, it can be expanded with loops, simulations, databases, APIs and specialist spatial packages. |


## Reproducibility 

```{r}
#| eval: false
result <- sites |>
  sf::st_buffer(dist = 500) |>
  sf::st_intersection(wetlands) |>
  dplyr::summarise(area = sum(sf::st_area(geometry)))

```


## Loops/re-use

```{r}
#| eval: false
process_catchment <- function(catchment, rivers, sites) {
  rivers |>
    sf::st_intersection(catchment) |>
    sf::st_join(sites)
}
results <- purrr::map(
  catchments,
  process_catchment,
  rivers = rivers,
  sites = sites
)

```
